q: Which of the following is a compulsory (EPI) vaccine in Sudan?
e: PCV is given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks; Hib is also in the EPI inside the pentavalent.

q: The following vaccines are live attenuated, EXCEPT:
All are contraindications to vaccination EXCEPT:
e: Antibiotic treatment is not a contraindication.

q: A woman positive for HBsAg delivers at term. The correct management of the newborn is:
o: Hepatitis B vaccine at 1 month only
Hepatitis B vaccine now and at 1 and 6 months only
HBIG only if cord blood is HBsAg positive
HBIG and hepatitis B vaccine within 12 hours, then complete the vaccine series
e: Both passive (HBIG) and active (vaccine) immunization at birth; breastfeeding is allowed.

q: All of the following should not receive oral polio vaccine EXCEPT:
e: Asymptomatic HIV-positive children receive all EPI vaccines.

q: Which statement about vaccines is correct?
o: Live vaccines are advised in symptomatic immunodeficiency
After anaphylaxis to a vaccine, give the next dose
BCG leaves a scar that confirms vaccination
e: BCG papule → ulcer → scar by 3 months. Varicella is live; anaphylaxis is a contraindication.

q: Contraindications to vaccination include all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Antibiotics, mild illness, diarrhoea and hospital admission are not contraindications.

q: Which of the following is true about the conjugated Hib vaccine?
o: Can be given from 2 months of age (6 weeks in the EPI)
Not given after a DPT reaction
e: Conjugation lets it work in infants; in Sudan it is in the pentavalent at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.
Measles vaccine is live: avoid in pregnancy. Malnourished children need it most.

q: Absolute contraindication to the pertussis vaccine:
o: Encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous dose
e: Encephalopathy after a previous dose or progressive neurological disease: give DT-HepB-Hib without pertussis.

q: In exams, which vaccine is linked to egg sensitivity?
e: MMR is grown in chick embryo culture (classic answer); in practice MMR is safe in egg allergy, while yellow fever and influenza need caution.

q: Which vaccine is contraindicated in an immunocompromised child?
e: Live vaccines (OPV, BCG, measles, rotavirus) are avoided; IPV is used instead.

q: A 4-month-old develops intussusception one week after a routine vaccine. The vaccine most associated is:
e: Rotavirus vaccine carries a very small risk of intussusception.

q: Which vaccine in the Sudan EPI is given intradermally?
e: BCG 0.05 ml intradermal; measles is subcutaneous; Penta, PCV and IPV are IM.

q: An infant has a painless left axillary node 2 months after BCG. He is well. The best management is:
e: Non-suppurative BCG lymphadenitis resolves; a fluctuant node is aspirated.

q: A 6-week-old has mild diarrhoea and a temperature of 37.6 °C on vaccination day. You should:
o: Give vaccines after an antibiotic course
e: Mild illness and low-grade fever are not contraindications.

q: A child missed the 10-week vaccines and comes at 6 months. The correct action is:
o: Continue the series from the missed dose
e: Never restart a series; continue with 4-week intervals.

q: Which vaccines are given at 9 months in the Sudan EPI?
e: 9 months: MR 1 + meningococcal A (yellow fever in states at risk); MR 2 at 18 months.
